title: Quantum critical fan and emergent relativistic symmetry of two-dimensional Dirac semimetals
authors: Friederike Ihssen, Bilal Hawashin, Mireia Tolosa-Simeón, Michael M. Scherer
abstract: Two-dimensional Dirac semimetals near a quantum critical point can be described by Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models. In view of recent experimental advances exhibiting a transition from Dirac semimetal to insulator in highly-tunable van-der-Waals heterostructures, a better understanding of finite-temperature effects is mandatory. Here, we study the Gross--Neveu--Yukawa phase diagram of the chiral Ising model with a non-perturbative field-theory approach at zero and finite temperature, both in the semimetallic phase and in the insulating phase with spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. At zero temperature, we find a quantum critical point with critical exponents that are close to the ones of the chiral Ising universality class, and show that relativistic symmetry is emergent close to the quantum critical point. At finite temperature, the ordered phase survives up to a finite critical temperature, at which we observe a classical phase transition into the disordered phase. We confirm that this transition lies in the two-dimensional Ising universality class. Finally, we determine the extent and scaling properties of the quantum critical fan, and the behavior of the quasiparticle weight, therein. In summary, we present a unified field-theoretical framework for the phase diagram of the chiral Ising model in the surroundings of its quantum critical point.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive field-theoretical framework using the functional renormalization group (fRG) to analyze the phase diagram of 2D Dirac semimetals near a quantum critical point. The study confirms that the system exhibits universal critical behavior belonging to the chiral Ising and 2D Ising universality classes at different temperature limits. It provides crucial insights into how relativistic symmetry can emerge in these strongly interacting electronic systems.
main_problem: The study aims to understand finite-temperature effects and the phase diagram of two-dimensional Dirac semimetals near a quantum critical point (QCP). This requires analyzing the Gross--Neveu--Yukawa model in both semimetallic and insulating regimes.
main_result: The authors find that at zero temperature, the QCP exhibits critical exponents matching the chiral Ising universality class, and relativistic symmetry emerges. At finite temperatures, a classical phase transition into the disordered phase belongs to the 2D Ising universality class.
method: The primary method employed is the non-perturbative functional renormalization group (fRG) approach applied to the effective field theory describing the system's dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system involves two-dimensional Dirac semimetals, modeled by the Gross--Neveu--Yukawa (GNY) model, which simplifies to the chiral Ising model. The Lagrangian describes interacting fermions coupled to a scalar order parameter field $\phi$.
key_observables: Critical exponents ($\alpha$), phase diagram boundaries, quasiparticle weight, and the extent of the quantum critical fan.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), coupling constants (e.g., $h\Lambda$), and proximity to the QCP.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a non-perturbative fRG treatment, which is used to map out the phase diagram across different temperature regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the GNY phase diagram and the Quantum Critical Fan (QCF), with color coding representing the calculated scaling exponent ($\alpha$) as a function of coupling ($h\Lambda$) and temperature ($T$).
paper_structure: The paper develops a unified field-theoretical framework by analyzing the system's behavior across different regimes: zero temperature QCP analysis, finite temperature classical transition analysis, and finally determining the scaling properties within the quantum critical fan.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter criticality, the use of advanced non-perturbative RG techniques to map out phase boundaries and emergent symmetries is highly relevant for understanding many-body dynamics in strongly correlated systems studied in AMO physics.
